questions.question: Under what condition is an entire object considered to be floating on water?
options: If the whole object is completely submerged under the water
If any part of the object remains above the surface of the water
Only if exactly half of the object is above the water
If the object sinks to the bottom but does not touch the floor

questions.question: If you place a toy boat in a shallow pond and then in a deep lake, how does the depth of the water affect how well it floats?
options: It floats better in the deep lake because there is more water.
It floats better in the shallow pond because the bottom is closer.
The depth of the liquid does not affect how well the object floats.
It will only float in water that is deeper than the height of the boat.

questions.question: What condition must be met for an object's shape to allow it to float in water?
options: Its shape must push its own mass of water out of the way without going under.
Its shape must be completely hollow and spherical.
Its shape must minimize contact with the water surface.
Its shape must trap air beneath it at all times.

questions.question: Approximately how much force is required to lift a 1 kg mass vertically on Earth?
options: 1 N

questions.question: What happens to the extension of a spring when you increase the force applied to it by equal-sized increments?
options: The extension increases by a larger amount with each step.
The extension increases by a smaller amount with each step.
The extension increases by the same amount for each equal-sized increase in force.
The extension remains constant regardless of the force applied.

questions.question: When a spring behaves elastically, what is the relationship between the force applied and its extension?
options: The extension is directly proportional to the force applied.
The extension is inversely proportional to the force applied.
The extension is equal to the square of the force applied.
There is no mathematical relationship between the force and extension.

questions.question: What makes a spring 'elastic'?
options: It can be stretched to twice its length without breaking.
It returns to its original length when the stretching force is removed.
It is made of a polymer material like rubber.
It requires a very small force to start stretching.

questions.question: What is a key function of a lever when used as a force multiplier?
options: It can multiply a small force into a larger force.
It can eliminate the need for a pivot entirely.
It reduces the distance over which a force must be applied.
It converts gravitational potential energy directly into kinetic energy.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the concept of pressure?
options: The total amount of force acting on an entire object
A measure of how concentrated a force is
The speed at which a force is applied to a surface
The mass of an object divided by its volume

questions.question: How is pressure calculated from force and area?
options: Pressure = force * area
Pressure = force / area
Pressure = area / force
Pressure = force + area

questions.question: What is another name for the unit 'newtons per square metre' (N/m²)?
options: Joule (J)
Watt (W)
Pascal (Pa)
Newton-metre (Nm)

questions.question: Why does water pressure increase as you dive deeper into a swimming pool?
options: Because the temperature of the water decreases.
Because there is more liquid pushing down.
Because the density of the water increases rapidly with depth.
Because the gravitational pull is stronger at the bottom of the pool.

questions.question: Why does atmospheric pressure reduce as you climb a high mountain?
options: Because there is less air pushing down.
Because the air temperature becomes much colder.
Because gravity is significantly weaker at high altitudes.
Because the speed of the wind increases with height.

questions.question: How does the extension of a rubber band behave compared to a spring when equal-sized increases in force are applied?
options: It increases by the same amount for each equal increase in force.
It increases by different amounts for each equal-sized increase in force.
It does not extend at all until a threshold force is reached.
It decreases in length as more force is applied.

questions.question: How is the moment of a force calculated?
options: Moment = force / distance from the pivot
Moment = force * perpendicular distance from the pivot
Moment = mass * acceleration due to gravity
Moment = force * area of the surface

questions.question: What is the standard unit of measurement for a moment?
options: Newtons (N)
Newton-metres (Nm)
Pascals (Pa)
Joules (J)
